statement.p:
Let P(x) be the predicate, 9x+1 is even.
Is P(13) true or false?
?
True
False
Neither (not a statement)
What, if anything, can you conclude about \exists x P(x) from the truth value of P(13)\text{?}
\exists x P(x) must be true.
\exists x P(x) must be false.
\exists x P(x) could be true or could be false.
What, if anything, can you conclude about \forall x P(x) from the truth value of P(13)\text{?}
\forall x P(x) must be true.
\forall x P(x) must be false.
\forall x P(x) could be true or could be false.

solution.p: P(13) is the statement 9\cdot 13 + 1 is even, which is true. Thus the statement \exists x P(x) is true (for example, 13 is such an x). However, we cannot tell anything about \forall x P(x) since we do not know the truth value of P(x) for all elements of the domain of discourse. In this case, \forall x P(x) happens to be false (since P(4) is false, for example).
